key_insight: An open-source hardware-and-software toolkit automates RHEED control and analysis so both humans and AI agents can guide thin-film growth in a more quantitative, reproducible way.
engineering_relevance: The toolkit lowers the barrier to agentic synthesis by adding programmable electron-optics control, automated alignment, and shared interfaces for analysis, enabling tighter integration of measurement, computation, and closed-loop process control.
method: Programmable RHEED electron-optics control with automated beam alignment and rocking-curve acquisition
Training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment for faster setup
Auto RHEED app with shared GUI and programmatic access, including an MCP server and extensible adapters for new AI/simulation methods
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a pulsed laser deposition system where natural-language requests guided the selection, configuration, and execution of quantitative RHEED analyses.
watch_item: The approach still depends on robust system-specific integration and the quality of future adapter methods, so performance may vary across different deposition platforms and materials systems.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
